answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, a smart-contract bond is created for each identity, locking its own refundable bond. This makes it costly for a single entity to create multiple identities. Only when cryptographic proof shows conflicting commitments signed for the same task does the bond get slashed. Like a prism refracting light, this mechanism filters out malicious activity, revealing the tide of true intentions. Just as the karst landscape is shaped by erosion, this system carves out a path for trustworthy interactions.
